text:
alex: Heads-up — during the thin-client inference rate-limit canary we started seeing surge 429s for our ml-small model in eu-west. First noticed ~10:32UTC.
devon: Got it, can you paste a sample request id and error payload?
alex: req=rc_84f9a2, response: 429 {"code":"rate_limited","retry_after":1.2}. Pattern: bursts from a handful of customers hitting short-lived fanout with ~100 concurrent short calls.
priya: Is this the new per-client soft-limit we rolled for canary? I thought canary only targeted 5% of traffic to avoid exactly this.
alex: It is the new policy (per-client QPS scaled down by 50%). Canary targeted 5% but traffic skewed: 3 customers in the canary produce most traffic. That concentrated load spiked per-client counters.
liam: Can you share the spectral of latency? 429s or slow tails?
alex: Mostly 429s right after request bursts. Median lat ok. Example trace: ``[10:32:11] req rc_84f9a2 start -> [10:32:11.2] 429``
priya: Opsbot, can you show rate-limit metrics for ml-small in eu-west for the last 30m?
opsbot: metric snapshot: rate.limiter.ml-small.eu-west.per_client_violations: 172 in 30m, top clients: cust-A(98), cust-C(43), cust-B(21). avg retry_after: 1.1s
devon: Sounds like per-client threshold too low for those customers' traffic patterns. Two options: widen per-client for canary or temporarily exclude top clients from canary.
alex: Excluding customers might be faster; we can flip exclusion list in the rollout config. Priya — do we have owners for cust-A/B/C to notify?
priya: I have owners for cust-A and cust-B. Cust-C is an internal test harness — maybe it's a rogue load generator hitting the canary. I'm pulling logs.
liam: If we exclude top clients, we should also increase soft-penalty window (from 1s -> 2s) to reduce 429 churn. Low lift to config.
devon: Agree. Proposal: 1) Pause further canary expansion. 2) Patch rollout config to exclude cust-A/B/C from canary group. 3) Increase soft penalty window to 2s and monitor for 15m. 4) If stable, resume with broader canary adjustments.
alex: I can patch the canary group now and flip the penalty. Will do the exclusion flip and report.
opsbot: Action log: canary.exclude updated by alex at 10:40UTC -> excluded cust-A,cust-B,cust-C. rate.limit.soft_window set to 2.0s by alex at 10:41UTC.
devon: Monitoring: any change in 5m, 15m windows?
opsbot: metric update at 10:46UTC: per_client_violations down to 21 in last 15m; top client now cust-D(9). 429 rate decreased by ~88%.
priya: Good, but we should root-cause cust-A behavior: their traffic is bursty but legitimate. Recommend follow-up: suggest client-side jitter/batching and add them to dedicated rate-tier if needed.
liam: Also schedule a quick postmortem doc: decision path, config changes, customers excluded, and recommendation for future canaries (ensure distribution check to avoid heavy skew).
alex: Agreed. I'll open a short postmortem and loop in sales/CS for cust-A/B.
devon: For rollback — not needed now, patch worked. But if any downstream product teams see anomalies, tag me.
priya: I'll keep watching logs for cust-C to confirm it's not an automation bug.
alex: Wrapping up: canary paused for expansion, exclusion applied, soft_window increased, monitoring healthy at 10:50UTC. Next steps: postmortem + customer outreach + tighter pre-canary traffic-distribution check.
liam: Thanks all :thumbsup:
priya: thanks
opsbot: Reminder: run canary-distribution-check script before next canary push.``
